issue.title: [http2] Keep remotely closed streams until their queues are done
issue.body_html:
Fixes #2021.

StreamHandler._handleEndOfStreamRemote removed a stream from _openStreams as soon as the peer's END_STREAM moved it from HalfClosedLocal to Closed, even if the application had not read the stream's incoming messages yet. The stream's entry in the connection-level ConnectionMessageQueueIn was left behind, so a later Connection._terminate skipped the stream (StreamHandler.onTerminated only walks _openStreams) and then failed:

Failed assertion: '_stream2messageQueue.isEmpty': is not true.
  ConnectionMessageQueueIn.onTerminated
  Connection._terminate

When END_STREAMs arrive in the other order (ours after the peer's), _endStream moves the stream to Closed without removing it. It stays in _openStreams until both of its queues are done and _cleanupClosedStream runs, so termination closes it normally. This change makes the peer-END_STREAM path behave the same way, which is what the TODO at that line was asking for.

Tests

terminate-with-undrained-closed-stream--{server,client}-ends-first in transport_test.dart runs the scenario from the issue over the in-memory transport, in both END_STREAM orders, with the server never reading the stream's messages:

Order Before After
server END_STREAM first ❌ assertion above ✅
client END_STREAM first ✅ ✅

The first commit adds only the test, so it can be checked out to see the failure. dart test in pkgs/http2 passes (256 tests), and dart analyze --fatal-infos reports no issues.

nodes.title: http2: Connection._terminate asserts _stream2messageQueue.isEmpty on a stream _handleEndOfStreamRemote orphaned

issue.title: http2: Connection._terminate asserts _stream2messageQueue.isEmpty on a stream _handleEndOfStreamRemote orphaned
issue.body_html:
What happens

ConnectionMessageQueueIn.onTerminated asserts that every stream has already
been unregistered:

// lib/src/flowcontrol/connection_queues.dart
@override
void onTerminated(Object? error) {
  // NOTE: The higher level will be shutdown first, so all streams
  // should have been removed at this point.
  assert(_stream2messageQueue.isEmpty);
  assert(_stream2pendingMessages.isEmpty);
  closeWithError(error);
}

That invariant can be broken by StreamHandler._handleEndOfStreamRemote, which
drops a fully-closed stream from _openStreams while deliberately keeping its
entry in the connection-level queue — the TODO directly above the line says so:

// lib/src/streams/stream_handler.dart
} else if (stream.state == StreamState.HalfClosedLocal) {
  _changeState(stream, StreamState.Closed);
  // TODO: We have to make sure that we
  //   - remove the stream for data structures which only care about the state
  //   - keep the stream in data structures which need to be emptied
  //     (e.g. MessageQueues which are not empty yet).
  _openStreams.remove(stream.id);
}

Connection._terminate then terminates _streams and only _openStreams
within it, before terminating the connection queue:

_streams.terminate(exception);     // iterates _openStreams only
_incomingQueue.terminate(exception);   // asserts the queue is empty

So any stream that reached Closed via _handleEndOfStreamRemote with messages
still undispatched is invisible to _streams.terminate and fails the assert.

Trigger

Two conditions together:

  1. The application never drains that stream's inbound messages, so the
    stream-level StreamMessageQueueIn stays buffered and the connection-level
    _tryDispatch never removes the entry.
  2. The server's END_STREAM is written before the client's END_STREAM is
    processed, so _handleEndOfStreamRemote sees HalfClosedLocal and takes the
    _openStreams.remove branch. In the reverse order the stream stays in
    _openStreams and teardown is clean.

Reproduction — deterministic, package:http2 only

Driving the frame order by hand, this fires 3/3 with A_FIRST and is clean 3/3
with B_FIRST:

// dart --enable-asserts repro.dart [A_FIRST|B_FIRST]
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:io';
import 'package:http2/transport.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  final aFirst = args.isEmpty || args.first == 'A_FIRST';
  final listener = await ServerSocket.bind(InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4, 0);
  ServerTransportConnection? serverConn;
  final serverReady = Completer<ServerTransportStream>();

  listener.listen((socket) {
    socket.setOption(SocketOption.tcpNoDelay, true);
    final conn = ServerTransportConnection.viaStreams(socket, socket);
    serverConn = conn;
    // Deliberately NOT listening to stream.incomingMessages: the application
    // never drains this stream.
    conn.incomingStreams.listen(serverReady.complete);
  });

  final clientSocket =
      await Socket.connect(InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4, listener.port);
  clientSocket.setOption(SocketOption.tcpNoDelay, true);
  final clientConn =
      ClientTransportConnection.viaStreams(clientSocket, clientSocket);

  final clientStream = clientConn.makeRequest([
    Header.ascii(':method', 'POST'),
    Header.ascii(':path', '/Repro/Fail'),
    Header.ascii(':scheme', 'http'),
    Header.ascii(':authority', 'localhost'),
  ], endStream: false);
  clientStream.incomingMessages.listen((_) {}, onError: (_) {});

  final serverStream = await serverReady.future;

  Future<void> a() async {   // server's END_STREAM
    serverStream.sendHeaders([Header.ascii('x-status', '16')], endStream: true);
    await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));
  }
  Future<void> b() async {   // client's END_STREAM
    clientStream.sendData([0, 0, 0, 0, 0], endStream: true);
    await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));
  }

  if (aFirst) { await a(); await b(); } else { await b(); await a(); }

  await serverConn!.finish();
  await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 200));
  await clientConn.terminate();
  await listener.close();
  exit(0);
}

A_FIRST produces:

'package:http2/src/flowcontrol/connection_queues.dart': Failed assertion: line 204 pos 12: '_stream2messageQueue.isEmpty': is not true.
  package:http2/src/flowcontrol/connection_queues.dart 204:12  ConnectionMessageQueueIn.onTerminated
  package:http2/src/error_handler.dart 17:7                    TerminatableMixin.terminate
  package:http2/src/connection.dart 437:22                     Connection._terminate
  package:http2/src/connection.dart 180:7                      Connection._setupConnection.<fn>

How we hit it in practice

Through package:grpc. Its server pauses the request subscription while the
interceptors run and its _sinkIncoming() never resumes it, so a refused call
satisfies condition 1 for every request; condition 2 then happens occasionally
under parallel load, and the assert reddened full CI runs about half the time.
I have filed that half separately against grpc/grpc-dart and it is the part we
are fixing on our side — but the invariant hole here is reachable by any caller
that leaves a stream's inbound messages undrained, which is why it seems worth
reporting on its own.

Suggested direction

Either have _handleEndOfStreamRemote keep the stream somewhere
_terminate can still find, or have _terminate sweep
_stream2messageQueue/_stream2pendingMessages before asserting. Happy to
attempt a PR if you have a preference between those.

Versions

http2 2.3.1 (reached via grpc 5.1.0, which constrains http2: ^2.3.1). Both
code sites verified unchanged on master at the time of filing, so 3.1.0 is
affected too.

issue.title: fix(http2): do not head-of-line block HEADERS, RST_STREAM and GOAWAY behind window-exhausted DATA
issue.body_html:
Note

This PR was generated by an AI coding agent (Jetski) on behalf of @mosuem.

Summary

ConnectionMessageQueueOut is a strict FIFO. Once the connection-level send window is exhausted, a DataMessage at the head of the queue blocks everything behind it, including frames that are not subject to flow control (RFC 9113 Section 6.9: "Flow control only applies to frames that are identified as being subject to flow control. Of the frame types defined in this document, this includes only DATA frames."). In practice: while one stream was waiting for WINDOW_UPDATE, no new request could be opened (HEADERS), no stream could be cancelled (RST_STREAM), and the connection could not be shut down gracefully (GOAWAY) until the peer granted credit.

Changes

  • lib/src/flowcontrol/connection_queues.dart:
    • _peekSendableMessage() replaces the "first message or nothing" rule. When the window is exhausted and the head of the queue is a DataMessage, it returns the first GOAWAY, or the first HEADERS / RST_STREAM whose stream has no earlier queued message. Skipping a message of a stream blocks every later message of that stream (and, for a PUSH_PROMISE, of the promised stream), so per-stream frame order is preserved: trailers never overtake their own DATA.
    • The scan is linear in the queue length, and StreamMessageQueueOut keeps forwarding DATA into this queue while the connection window is exhausted (it only checks the stream window). To avoid rescanning on every sendData() call, enqueueMessage skips _trySendMessages() when a DataMessage is enqueued while _connectionWindow.positiveWindow.wouldBuffer is true (since the new DataMessage cannot be sent and cannot unblock any earlier queued message). Enqueueing a non-DATA message while blocked still costs one pass over the queue.

Test Verification (Fails Before $\rightarrow$ Passes After)

Added to test/client_test.dart:

  • headers-and-rst-not-blocked-or-reordered-on-exhausted-window: stream 1 exhausts the connection window; stream 3's HEADERS and stream 5's HEADERS + RST_STREAM must still go out, in that order, before the window is replenished.
  • trailers-stay-behind-blocked-data-while-other-headers-bypass: stream 1 has blocked DATA and queued trailers; stream 3's HEADERS bypass them, stream 1's trailers are only written after its DATA.

Before fix:

00:05 +0 -1: client-tests client-errors headers-and-rst-not-blocked-or-reordered-on-exhausted-window [E]
  TimeoutException after 0:00:05.000000: Test timed out after 5 seconds.
00:10 +0 -2: client-tests client-errors trailers-stay-behind-blocked-data-while-other-headers-bypass [E]
  TimeoutException after 0:00:05.000000: Test timed out after 5 seconds.

(stream 3's HEADERS never leave the client while stream 1 waits for credit)

After fix:

00:00 +2: All tests passed!
